\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{corollary}{Corollary}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{Partition Repair Maps and Exact Weighted Congestion}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We give the exact finite theorem needed to convert a geometric repair of bad configurations into a normalized weighted partition-numerator bound, retaining multiplicity, state weight, and Jacobian loss.\end{abstract}
Let $T:B\to G$ map bad states to good states. For good weights $g_y$, bad weights $b_x$, present weight $V(s)$, and next-state weight $V(\tau x)$, define
\[C_T=\max_{y\in G}\frac{\sum_{x:T(x)=y}b_xV(\tau x)}{g_yV(s)}.\]
\begin{theorem}[Exact repair congestion]The weighted bad numerator obeys
\[B_V(s)\le C_T Z_G(s)V(s).\]
Thus the ratio to the good partition is at most $C_T$.\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}Group the bad sum by repair fibers and apply the definition of $C_T$ to each good state before summing.\end{proof}
\begin{corollary}If every repair fiber has at most $M$ elements and each repaired density ratio, including state and Jacobian factors, is at most $e^{J-\Delta}$, then
\[C_T\le Me^{J-\Delta},\qquad F_T\ge\Delta-J-\log M.\]
\end{corollary}
Exponential repair multiplicity can cancel an action drop, reproducing the mandatory entropy counterexample.
\begin{remark}The theorem gives the exact normalization interface. A nonlinear, gauge-covariant $SU(2)$ repair with uniform congestion remains open.\end{remark}\end{document}
